clue.text: Good opening with scope for clever move

indicators.note: the opening of the word Good is its first letter, so only that letter is taken

parts.note: ambit means scope or extent

explanation.surface: A promising chess opening that gives a player room for a smart move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good opening' looks like the definition, since a gambit is a chess opening, but 'opening' here picks the first letter of 'Good'; the definition is 'clever move'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambit is a calculated opening ploy, so it is a crafty manoeuvre made to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Fitted top removed from piece of furniture

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of the word is its first letter, and that letter is taken off

parts.note: a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A fitted piece of furniture that has had its top taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitted can mean suited or qualified for something, which is a sense of capable.

clue.text: Bound to go on the wagon

parts.note: to buck is to leap or bound, as a horse does
to board a vehicle is to go on it

explanation.surface: Someone sure to give up drink and go on the wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to go on the wagon' reads as being certain to stop drinking; in fact 'wagon' is the definition. A buckboard is an American four-wheeled open carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A buckboard is a light open horse-drawn wagon whose seat rests on a flexible board.

clue.text: Fuss about the French in Spanish city

indicators.note: about means around, so the fuss word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or commotion
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Some commotion over the French presence in a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic city in central Spain, famous for its swords.

clue.text: Criminal picked up in response to telephone call

definitions.meaning: a criminal who handles stolen goods, a fence

definitions.text: picked up in response to telephone call
definitions.meaning: the handset you lift when the phone rings

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: a receiver of stolen goods is a criminal, and the receiver is the part of a telephone you lift to answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fence who handles stolen property and the handset of a telephone.

clue.text: Got back to front

parts.note: reads as reversed, but means a competitor who had been overtaken returned to first place

explanation.walkthrough: 'Back to front' suggests something reversed; read it instead as getting back to the front of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To return to first position after falling behind is to recover one's position at the head of the field.

clue.text: Stepping stones to reason and method

parts.note: a cause is a reason
a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: Small steps leading towards reason and method, like a philosopher's path.
explanation.definitionFit: A causeway is a raised path across water or marsh, as a line of stepping stones is.

clue.text: Not flush, but accepted by the social clique

parts.note: to be in with a group is to be accepted by it
the set is a fashionable social group

explanation.surface: Someone short of money yet still welcomed by the smart crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not flush' suggests being short of cash, but here it means not level with a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set into a surface is recessed rather than level with it.

clue.text: I represent change — it's what's wanted in industry

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A business leader who says he stands for change, the very quality commerce needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Initiative and resourcefulness, the spirit of starting new ventures, is what business prizes.

clue.text: He won't go out with his mates

definitions.text: He won't go out with his mates

parts.words: He won't go out with his mates
parts.note: suggests a social loner, but going out means going on strike with fellow workers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go out' means to strike: a strikebreaker keeps working while his colleagues walk out.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackleg is a worker who refuses to join a strike, so he stays at work when colleagues stop.

clue.text: Troubles with top dentures?

definitions.meaning: disturbs or worries, as a verb
upper false teeth, read as two words, sets that go up

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into UP SETS, sets of false teeth for the upper jaw.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb is to upset; read as two words, upper sets of false teeth.

clue.text: A relation in retirement

parts.note: suggests a relative who has retired, but means something related, or told, as one retires for the night

explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' means a telling or narrative, and 'retirement' means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale read to a child at the end of the day is a narration given at the hour of going to bed.

clue.text: It's appropriate to support unhappy sort of worker

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so the unhappy word goes underneath the other

parts.note: blue means sad or unhappy
to collar is to seize or appropriate something

explanation.surface: Someone sad propping up a fitting kind of worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: A manual or industrial worker is described by this term, from the work shirts traditionally worn.

clue.text: Mid-off on field in repulsive jumper

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed next to, so the next piece follows
mid asks for the middle letter of the word it is attached to

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder at mid-off, out on the field, spotting a nasty insect hopping.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-off is a cricket fielding position, but here 'Mid-' picks the middle letter of 'off'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a parasitic insect that leaps prodigiously, so it is an unpleasant jumper.

clue.text: Charms the French in love affairs

parts.note: en is the French word for in
amours are love affairs

explanation.surface: The French have a charming way with romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French in' asks for the French word for 'in', not the French word for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to captivate them, to fill them with love.

clue.text: Former pupil's term in complex

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school
a session is a term, as of a court or school

explanation.surface: An old boy's school term spent in a complicated building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' looks like an adjective but is the psychological noun.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychology a complex is a fixation, an idea that preoccupies the mind.

clue.text: Clever head raises enthusiasm

parts.note: keen means sharp or clever, as in a keen mind
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A bright headteacher stirs up eagerness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' is a headland, NESS, as in Loch Ness's neighbour place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagerness or zeal is a state of being eager, which is the abstract noun for enthusiasm.

clue.text: Preliminary race neither quick nor decisive

definitions.text: Preliminary race neither quick nor decisive

parts.note: the quick and the dead: not quick, that is not living, means dead
a heat is a preliminary race

explanation.surface: A qualifying race that was slow and settled nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' is used in its old sense of alive, as in 'the quick and the dead'; the whole clue describes a tied race.
explanation.definitionFit: A race in which two finish level is a tie, so it decides nothing.

clue.text: Twice as fair

indicators.note: twice says the piece is written two times in a row

parts.note: so means as, in comparisons such as 'not so big'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' means middling, not just or blond.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling or mediocre quality is described as only fair.

clue.text: Digs out stories that make the headlines

definitions.meaning: removes with a spoon or shovel
exclusive news stories one paper gets first

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: to dig out with a shovel, and newspaper exclusives.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means hollowing out with a ladle-like tool, and exclusive news reports.

clue.text: Ladies and gentlemen serving the public

definitions.text: Ladies and gentlemen serving the public

parts.words: Ladies and gentlemen serving the public
parts.note: suggests staff at work, but Ladies and Gents are the signs on public toilets

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' and 'Gents' are the signs on British public toilets, which are called public conveniences.
explanation.definitionFit: Public lavatories in Britain are formally called public conveniences, labelled Ladies and Gentlemen.

clue.text: Top scorer's off drive

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, telling us to rearrange the letters of drive

explanation.surface: A leading goalscorer has a stroke in cricket, an off drive.
explanation.walkthrough: An off drive is a cricket stroke, but 'off' is the anagram signal and 'Top scorer' means a great composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorer is someone who writes musical scores, and Verdi is among the greatest opera composers.

clue.text: Social worker takes one to be an opponent

parts.note: an ant is a social insect and a worker
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A social worker takes on a case and becomes an adversary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' is a worker ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is against something is an opponent; the word is used as a noun for such a person.

clue.text: Loafer vandalised plants

indicators.note: vandalised means wrecked, so the letters of loafer are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An idler wrecked the flower beds.
explanation.definitionFit: Florae is a plural of flora, the plant life of a region.

clue.text: Feelings shown by people put into some distress

definitions.text: Feelings shown by people put into some distress

parts.words: Feelings shown by people put into some distress
parts.note: describes how people react when upset

explanation.definitionFit: Feelings such as grief and fear are what people display when distressed.

clue.text: When parted, is upset, went for long walk

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters of parted and is are rearranged

explanation.surface: After a separation, someone distraught went off on a long trudge.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily a long way, so traipsed means trudged.

clue.text: Sombre at first and dark, but not in shadow

indicators.note: at first picks out the opening letter of Sombre

parts.note: unlit means dark

explanation.surface: Gloomy and dark at first, but later the scene brightens.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bathed in sunshine is brightly lit and so out of the shade.
